title: Can you look like an Olympic weightlifter naturally?
summary: NH examines whether a natural can achieve the physique of an Olympic weightlifter. He argues the snatch and clean and jerk are among the worst lifts for hypertrophy (explosive, no eccentric, low reps, highly technical) and that lifters' looks come partly from drugs and are a byproduct of performance. The look is achievable naturally by 'dehybridizing' the lifts into their component patterns or 'bastardizing' them (power/hang/block variations, snatch-grip pulls).
claims: The Olympic weightlifter physiques people covet are mostly in the 160-190 lb classes; super heavyweights tend to be fatter and less aesthetic
Oly lifters look aesthetic because specific areas are very developed: core/six-pack, shoulders, upper back
Elite Oly lifters never trained for looks; their physique is a byproduct of training for performance from a young age
You cannot take the path of function to arrive at form; chasing performance to obtain aesthetics is a waste of time
You don't need a 700 lb deadlift to have a big back; that powerlifter could have had a bigger back with a smaller deadlift
Much of what makes top Oly lifters look so good is drug use, not their regimen; physiques have visibly changed versus 20-30 years ago
The Oly lifter shape is still achievable naturally, just not by Olympic lifting
Oly lifters typically have relatively weak chests and strong shoulders because they do a lot of vertical pressing and almost no horizontal pressing
Oly lifters have very developed upper and lower backs from heavy pulls and thoracic extension demands, big quads, developed glutes and big necks
Ranked for hypertrophy, the snatch and clean and jerk sit at the very bottom; they were designed to be easy to judge and demonstrate power, not build muscle
Explosive lifts waste hypertrophy potential: the lifter tosses the bar and is not resisting it for much of the lift, while a bodybuilder wants to stay in control of the bar
The Olympic lifts are essentially positive-only; the catch and drop remove the eccentric, which is the portion most important for hypertrophy
Competitive Oly lifting works around single reps, but bodybuilding is built through repetitions
Using leg drive (jerk/push press) to lift more overhead doesn't build bigger shoulders; it unloads the shoulders by sharing work with the legs
Bodybuilders should not invest time developing technique for lifts that are subpar for hypertrophy; every technical lift is an investment that must pay back in growth
Chinese lifters reportedly spend two to three years mostly drilling technique before loading heavily
You don't spend three years learning to curl; you spend ten minutes and then curl
Highly technical lifts are 'jealous': the higher the technical rating, the faster the skill decays, so they must be programmed constantly or you can't load them enough to damage muscle
Using Olympic lifts to develop athletes' power is counterproductive; most football players perform the clean with terrible front racks and wrist positions and test one-rep maxes
The clean and jerk can be brute-forced while the snatch can't, which is why coaches rarely program snatches for athletes and a sign the technical rating is too high
Dehybridization: split a complex lift into its parts; the clean and jerk becomes a pull, a front squat and an overhead press
Separating the clean and jerk into components is less time-efficient but around five times better for hypertrophy
Front squats may not be the best option for bodybuilders because they are too technical
Bastardization: cut the range of motion to reduce technicality, e.g. power cleans, cleans from a rack/hang, snatches from blocks
Replace snatches with snatch-grip deadlifts to get the posterior-chain benefits of the pull without putting the bar overhead
NH does a lot of snatch-grip deadlifts and snatch-grip work because a wide grip is excellent for upper back development
You can look similar to an Oly lifter naturally, though maybe not as lean or muscular at their bodyweight
'To look like an athlete, train like an athlete' is nonsense; isolating the hypertrophic benefits of movement patterns is far faster, e.g. lift for a swimmer's physique rather than swim
Look at what athletes do, keep only what matters for aesthetics and throw the rest away
